significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that a linearly decodable “being evaluated vs. deployed” representation causally changes “refusal rate, honesty, and compliance”; this is principally a form-(ii) causal claim of the separable-direction-plus-steering-repair shape, not a quantitative law. It would establish both a behavioral phenomenon—safer behavior under perceived evaluation—and a mechanism linking that shift to one internal direction, constraining explanations of context-dependent safety behavior highlighted by Greenblatt et al.’s alignment-faking work and Laine et al.’s Situational Awareness Dataset, but it remains bounded to one broad behavioral failure family. Verified false would distinguishably rule out a unitary, linearly accessible causal substrate as stated, though it would not rule out nonlinear, distributed, or cue-specific evaluation awareness, so the negative branch is only moderately informative. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic mechanistic LLM safety would not supply the specific evaluation/deployment context variable, but the claim is still close to the topic’s standard probe-and-steer template.

reach.justification: The named handle is “monitoring or ablating this direction during evaluation,” a diagnostic and intervention intended to produce more deployment-representative safety measurements. Monitoring is ex ante with respect to deployment because an auditor could flag evaluation-conditioned compliance before shipping, while ablation is an evaluation-time knob; this gives uptake to safety evaluators and deployment gatekeepers rather than only mechanistic-interpretability researchers. After per-model re-extraction, the asserted correlation between representation strength and the “behavioral eval/deploy gap” predicts a qualitative relation, but no transferable threshold or quantitative law, and the broad “LLMs” scope is vulnerable to cue, architecture, and training-recipe dependence. The topic-substitution check fails to retain the score: without the evaluation-awareness direction, the topic alone provides neither this pre-deployment diagnostic nor its specific auditing action window.
